mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signal a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 110), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced corporate output and profit margins, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) over the past month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances with PAYEMS growth, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 350,000), the S&P 500 tends to outperform due to robust corporate revenue growth, leading to positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS > 350000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a broad-based supply shock that reduces corporate output and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a 3-year rolling window.
